witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 24.1
div.ab: Super barones socnam suam habentes habet iudex fiscalis iusticie legis obseruanciam, et quicquid peccabitur in eorum personam; nemo enim forisfacturam sui ipsius habuerit, set fortasse dominus eius.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 561 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: keiner [obwohl Jurisdictionsbesitzer] besitzt Gericht sammt Strafgeld (auch nicht ouerseunessam 36, 1) für Vergehen gegen seine eigene Person, sondern die Instanz über ihm
none [although holding jurisdiction] has the court together with the fine (not even ouerseunessam 36, 1) for offences against his own person; rather, the instance above him has it
gebessert vom Corr. aus fissc. Sc
corrected by the corrector from fissc. Sc
besser zu streichen; et si quid Lond
better deleted; et si quid Lond
so Co Or; habuit the others
Vgl. o. 20, 3; fortasse: ‘eventuell’—fischalis{46}—et{47} si quid p.—n.{37} f. ohne enim—habuit{48} Rs
Cf. above 20, 3; fortasse: ‘possibly’—fischalis{46}—et{47} si quid p.—n.{37} f. without enim—habuit{48} Rs

div.ab: Over barons having their soke the judge of fiscal justice has the observance of the law, and whatever wrong is done against their person; for no one will have the forfeiture of [an offence against] himself, but perhaps his lord.
